# kubectl-nv Documentation

## Overview

`kubectl-nv` is a kubectl plugin for troubleshooting NVIDIA GPU
resources in Kubernetes clusters. It never changes Kubernetes objects.
Today it provides one command, `kubectl nv adm must-gather`, which
collects a diagnostic bundle from a cluster where the NVIDIA GPU
Operator is deployed. Gathering it runs `nvidia-bug-report.sh` inside
the driver pods, which needs permission to create `pods/exec`.

## Quick Start

Install a released binary from the
[GitHub release page](https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv/releases), or build
from source:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv.git
cd kubectl-nv
make build
./bin/kubectl-nv --help
```

Either way, see [Installation](installation.md) for verifying the download and
putting `kubectl-nv` on your `PATH` so that `kubectl nv` resolves.

## Architecture

```mermaid
graph TD
    CLI[kubectl-nv CLI]
    subgraph Core
      ADM[adm command]
      MG[must-gather]
      LOG[logger]
    end
    K8S[Kubernetes API]
    CRD[Custom Resources]
    CLI --> ADM
    ADM --> MG
    MG -->|collects| K8S
    MG -->|fetches| CRD
    ADM --> LOG
    MG --> LOG
```

- [Installation](installation.md)

# Installation

## From the GitHub release page

Every release publishes a `tar.gz` archive per operating system and
architecture, a checksums file and an SBOM, on the
[release page](https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv/releases).

Pick the archive that matches your machine:

| Operating system | Architecture | Archive |
|---|---|---|
| Linux | x86_64 | `kubectl-nv_<version>_linux_amd64.tar.gz` |
| Linux | arm64 | `kubectl-nv_<version>_linux_arm64.tar.gz` |
| macOS | Intel | `kubectl-nv_<version>_darwin_amd64.tar.gz` |
| macOS | Apple silicon | `kubectl-nv_<version>_darwin_arm64.tar.gz` |

If you are not sure which architecture you have, run `uname -sm`.

### Download and verify

Download the archive and the `kubectl-nv_<version>_checksums.txt` file into the
same directory, then check the archive against it:

```bash
VERSION=0.1.0
OS=linux          # or darwin
ARCH=amd64        # or arm64

curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv/releases/download/v${VERSION}/kubectl-nv_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz"
curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv/releases/download/v${VERSION}/kubectl-nv_${VERSION}_checksums.txt"

# Linux
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing kubectl-nv_${VERSION}_checksums.txt

# macOS
shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing kubectl-nv_${VERSION}_checksums.txt
```

The line for your archive must read `OK`. Without `--ignore-missing` the check
fails on every archive you did not download.

### Put it on your PATH

kubectl finds a plugin by looking for an executable named `kubectl-nv` on your
`PATH`, which is what makes `kubectl nv` work:

```bash
tar -xzf kubectl-nv_${VERSION}_${OS}_${ARCH}.tar.gz kubectl-nv
chmod +x kubectl-nv
sudo install -m 0755 kubectl-nv /usr/local/bin/kubectl-nv
```

If you would rather not use `sudo`, move it into any directory that is already
on your `PATH`, for example `~/.local/bin`.

### Confirm

```bash
kubectl plugin list
```

`kubectl-nv` appears in the output. Then:

```bash
kubectl nv --version
kubectl nv adm must-gather --help
```

On macOS the first run may be blocked by Gatekeeper because the binary is not
notarized. Clear the quarantine attribute with
`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /usr/local/bin/kubectl-nv`.

## From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv.git
cd kubectl-nv
make build
./bin/kubectl-nv --help
```

Copy `bin/kubectl-nv` onto your `PATH` as above to use it through kubectl.

## Prerequisites

- `kubectl`, and a kubeconfig for the cluster you want to inspect
- The NVIDIA GPU Operator deployed in that cluster. `must-gather` locates the
  operator by its `app=gpu-operator` pods and fails if it finds none
- Permission to create `pods/exec` in the operator's namespace, because
  `must-gather` runs `nvidia-bug-report.sh` inside the driver pods
- Go, only for building from source. The version is the one in
  `deployments/devel/Dockerfile`

## Krew

kubectl-nv is not in a krew index yet. Install it from the release page or from
source until it is.

name: Golang

on:
  workflow_call: {}
  pull_request:
    types:
      - opened
      - synchronize
    branches:
      - main
      - release-*

jobs:
  variables:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      GOLANG_VERSION: ${{ steps.go_version.outputs.GOLANG_VERSION }}
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      name: Checkout code

    - name: Get Golang version
      id: go_version
      run: |
        GOLANG_VERSION=$(./hack/golang-version.sh)
        echo "GOLANG_VERSION=${GOLANG_VERSION##GOLANG_VERSION := }" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: variables
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      name: Checkout code

    - name: Install Go
      uses: actions/setup-go@v6
      with:
        go-version: ${{ needs.variables.outputs.GOLANG_VERSION }}

    - name: Lint
      uses: golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9
      with:
        version: latest
        args: -v --timeout 5m
        skip-cache: true

    - name: Check golang modules
      run: | 
        make check-vendor

  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: variables
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Get Golang version
        id: vars
        run: |
          GOLANG_VERSION=$(./hack/golang-version.sh)
          echo "GOLANG_VERSION=${GOLANG_VERSION##GOLANG_VERSION ?= }" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Install Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: ${{ needs.variables.outputs.GOLANG_VERSION }}

      - run: make build

  test:
    name: Unit test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: variables
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with:
          go-version: ${{ needs.variables.outputs.GOLANG_VERSION }}
  
      - run: make coverage
        name: Run unit tests and generate coverage report
  
      - name: Upload to Coveralls
        uses: coverallsapp/github-action@v2
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          file: coverage.out

name: Stale issues and pull requests

on:
  schedule:
  - cron: "21 4 * * *"

jobs:
  stale:
    permissions:
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/stale@v10
      with:
        stale-issue-message: 'This issue is stale because it has been open 90 days with no activity. This issue will be closed in 30 days unless new comments are made or the stale label is removed.'
        stale-pr-message: 'This PR is stale because it has been open 90 days with no activity. This PR will be closed in 30 days unless new comments are made or the stale label is removed.'
        stale-issue-label: 'lifecycle/stale'
        stale-pr-label: 'lifecycle/stale'
        days-before-stale: 90
        close-issue-message: 'This issue was automatically closed due to inactivity.'
        close-pr-message: 'This pull request was automatically closed due to inactivity.' 
        days-before-issue-close: 30
        days-before-pr-close: 30
        remove-stale-when-updated: true
        operations-per-run: 300

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'

# The write grant lives on the release job alone; everything else reads.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  variables:
    # Forks inherit the workflow but must not try to cut NVIDIA releases.
    if: github.repository == 'NVIDIA/kubectl-nv'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      GOLANG_VERSION: ${{ steps.go_version.outputs.GOLANG_VERSION }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Get Golang version
        id: go_version
        run: |
          GOLANG_VERSION=$(./hack/golang-version.sh)
          echo "GOLANG_VERSION=${GOLANG_VERSION##GOLANG_VERSION := }" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  release:
    if: github.repository == 'NVIDIA/kubectl-nv'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: variables
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with:
          # GoReleaser builds the changelog from the commits since the previous
          # tag, so it needs the full history and every tag.
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Nothing here pushes; GoReleaser uploads through the API token below.
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install Go
        uses: actions/setup-go@924ae3a1cded613372ab5595356fb5720e22ba16 # v6
        with:
          go-version: ${{ needs.variables.outputs.GOLANG_VERSION }}

      - name: Install syft
        uses: anchore/sbom-action/download-syft@e22c389904149dbc22b58101806040fa8d37a610 # v0

      - name: Run GoReleaser
        uses: goreleaser/goreleaser-action@f06c13b6b1a9625abc9e6e439d9c05a8f2190e94 # v7
        with:
          version: '~> v2'
          args: release --clean
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# NVIDIA kubectl-nv

`kubectl nv` is a kubectl plugin for the people who operate NVIDIA GPU
clusters. It runs on your machine with the kubeconfig and the RBAC you already
have, installs nothing in the cluster, and works on any distribution where the
NVIDIA GPU Operator is deployed. It never changes Kubernetes objects: today it
collects the diagnostic bundle that support asks for, so you do not have to run
the troubleshooting commands and the must-gather script by hand. Collecting
that bundle runs `nvidia-bug-report.sh` inside the driver pods, which needs
permission to create `pods/exec`.

## Install

Download a binary from the
[GitHub release page](https://github.com/NVIDIA/kubectl-nv/releases), verify it
against the checksums file, and put `kubectl-nv` on your `PATH` so that
`kubectl nv` resolves. Full instructions, including building from source, are
in [docs/installation.md](docs/installation.md).

## Commands

### kubectl nv adm must-gather

Collects the information from your cluster that is most likely needed for
debugging issues.

```bash
kubectl nv adm must-gather --artifacts-dir /tmp/support
```

```text
OPTIONS:
   --kubeconfig value, -k value  path to kubeconfig file (default: "-") [$KUBECONFIG]
   --artifacts-dir value         path to the directory where the artifacts will be stored. Defaults to /tmp/nvidia-gpu-operator_<timestamp> [$ARTIFACT_DIR]
   --help, -h                    show help
```

#!/bin/bash
# Copyright 2026 NVIDIA CORPORATION
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
#     http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
# limitations under the License.
#
# Tests for hack/lint-words.sh.
#
# The forbidden byte sequences and words are built with printf escapes so that
# this file does not itself contain anything lint-words.sh rejects.
#
# Exit codes under test: 0 clean, 1 findings, 2 the check could not run.
#
# lint-words.sh has two modes. Inside a git work tree it scans tracked files
# only; anywhere else it walks the tree. Both are exercised below, because a
# fixture that covers only one leaves the other unguarded.

set -u

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
LINT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/lint-words.sh"

EM_DASH="$(printf '\xe2\x80\x94')"
EN_DASH="$(printf '\xe2\x80\x93')"
BANNED_GPU="$(printf 'M\x6fck GPU')"
BANNED_LIB="$(printf 'libc\x75da')"
BANNED_SIM="$(printf 'DSX S\x69m')"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lint-words-test.XXXXXX")" || {
    echo "cannot create a temporary directory"
    exit 2
}
trap 'rm -rf "${WORK}"' EXIT

failures=0
cases=0

# run_case <name> <expected-rc> <fixture-root>
run_case() {
    local name="$1" expected="$2" root="$3"
    local log="${WORK}/$(echo "${name}" | tr ' /' '__').log"
    cases=$((cases + 1))

    bash "${LINT}" "${root}" > "${log}" 2>&1
    local rc=$?

    if [ "${rc}" -eq "${expected}" ]; then
        echo "PASS ${name} (rc=${rc})"
    else
        echo "FAIL ${name}: want rc=${expected}, got rc=${rc}"
        sed 's/^/    /' "${log}"
        failures=$((failures + 1))
    fi
}

# A plain directory, so lint-words.sh walks it. Every fixture carries a clean,
# in-scope file so that a tree is never empty.
new_tree() {
    local root
    root="$(mktemp -d "${WORK}/tree.XXXXXX")" || exit 2
    printf '# Title\n\nA clean line of prose.\n' > "${root}/clean.md"
    echo "${root}"
}

# A git work tree, so lint-words.sh scans tracked files only. The clean file is
# staged; each caller decides what to track beyond that.
new_repo() {
    local root
    root="$(mktemp -d "${WORK}/repo.XXXXXX")" || exit 2
    git -C "${root}" init -q > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
    printf '# Title\n\nA clean line of prose.\n' > "${root}/clean.md"
    git -C "${root}" add clean.md > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
    echo "${root}"
}

#
# Patterns. One fixture per alternative, so dropping any one of them is caught.
#

# 1. An em dash in a markdown file is rejected.
t1="$(new_tree)"
printf 'A sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${t1}/doc.md"
run_case "em dash in .md" 1 "${t1}"

# 2. An en dash in a Go file is rejected.
t2="$(new_tree)"
printf 'package main\n\n// Range 1 %s 9.\nfunc main() {}\n' "${EN_DASH}" > "${t2}/main.go"
run_case "en dash in .go" 1 "${t2}"

# 3. A banned device phrase in a YAML file is rejected, case-insensitively.
t3="$(new_tree)"
printf 'metadata:\n  description: "%s node"\n' "${BANNED_GPU}" > "${t3}/config.yaml"
run_case "banned device phrase in .yaml" 1 "${t3}"

# 4. The banned driver library name is rejected.
t4="$(new_tree)"
printf 'The plugin does not link against %s at all.\n' "${BANNED_LIB}" > "${t4}/doc.md"
run_case "banned library name in .md" 1 "${t4}"

# 5. The banned simulator name is rejected, case-insensitively.
t5="$(new_tree)"
printf 'Tested on the %s rig.\n' "${BANNED_SIM}" > "${t5}/doc.md"
run_case "banned simulator name in .md" 1 "${t5}"

#
# File types in scope.
#

# 6. Shell scripts are scanned.
t6="$(new_tree)"
printf '#!/bin/bash\n# step one %s step two\necho hello\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${t6}/script.sh"
run_case "em dash in .sh" 1 "${t6}"

# 7. The .yml spelling is scanned as well as .yaml.
t7="$(new_tree)"
printf 'name: CI\n# a comment %s with a long dash\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${t7}/workflow.yml"
run_case "em dash in .yml" 1 "${t7}"

# 8. A tree with nothing forbidden passes.
t8="$(new_tree)"
printf 'package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n' > "${t8}/main.go"
printf 'metadata:\n  name: kubectl-nv\n' > "${t8}/config.yaml"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho hello\n' > "${t8}/script.sh"
run_case "clean tree" 0 "${t8}"

#
# Directories out of scope when walking a plain tree.
#

# 9. Dependencies are not ours to rewrite.
t9="$(new_tree)"
mkdir -p "${t9}/vendor/example.com/pkg"
printf 'A vendored sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" \
    > "${t9}/vendor/example.com/pkg/README.md"
run_case "em dash only under vendor" 0 "${t9}"

# 10. Git's own store holds old blobs and commit messages.
t10="$(new_tree)"
mkdir -p "${t10}/.git/info"
printf 'A sentence %s from an old revision.\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${t10}/.git/info/notes.md"
run_case "em dash only under .git" 0 "${t10}"

# 11. GoReleaser output is a build artifact.
t11="$(new_tree)"
mkdir -p "${t11}/dist/kubectl-nv_linux_amd64"
printf 'A built sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" \
    > "${t11}/dist/kubectl-nv_linux_amd64/README.md"
run_case "em dash only under dist" 0 "${t11}"

# 12. A generated code graph is not source either.
t12="$(new_tree)"
mkdir -p "${t12}/graphify-out"
printf 'A generated sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" \
    > "${t12}/graphify-out/GRAPH_REPORT.md"
run_case "em dash only under graphify-out" 0 "${t12}"

#
# Inside a git work tree only tracked files count.
#

# 13. An untracked file is somebody's scratch space, not what the repo ships.
r13="$(new_repo)"
printf 'A scratch sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${r13}/scratch.md"
run_case "untracked em dash in a git tree" 0 "${r13}"

# 14. The same file once it is staged is part of the repository.
r14="$(new_repo)"
printf 'A staged sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${r14}/staged.md"
git -C "${r14}" add staged.md > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "tracked em dash in a git tree" 1 "${r14}"

# 15. Tracked dependencies stay out of scope in a git tree too.
r15="$(new_repo)"
mkdir -p "${r15}/vendor/example.com/pkg"
printf 'A vendored sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" \
    > "${r15}/vendor/example.com/pkg/README.md"
git -C "${r15}" add vendor > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "tracked em dash under vendor in a git tree" 0 "${r15}"

# 16. Tracked shell scripts are scanned in a git tree.
r16="$(new_repo)"
printf '#!/bin/bash\n# step one %s step two\necho hello\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${r16}/script.sh"
git -C "${r16}" add script.sh > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "tracked em dash in .sh in a git tree" 1 "${r16}"

# 17. So are tracked .yml files.
r17="$(new_repo)"
printf 'name: CI\n# a comment %s with a long dash\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${r17}/workflow.yml"
git -C "${r17}" add workflow.yml > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "tracked em dash in .yml in a git tree" 1 "${r17}"

# 18. A git tree with nothing forbidden passes.
r18="$(new_repo)"
printf 'package main\n\nfunc main() {}\n' > "${r18}/main.go"
git -C "${r18}" add main.go > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "clean git tree" 0 "${r18}"

# 19. Tracked Go sources are scanned in a git tree.
r19="$(new_repo)"
printf 'package main\n\n// Range 1 %s 9.\nfunc main() {}\n' "${EN_DASH}" > "${r19}/main.go"
git -C "${r19}" add main.go > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "tracked en dash in .go in a git tree" 1 "${r19}"

# 20. A git tree with nothing in scope has nothing to report. The checker must
# reach that answer, not fall through to scanning the whole tree.
r20="$(new_repo)"
git -C "${r20}" rm -q --cached clean.md > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
printf 'A loose sentence %s with a long dash.\n' "${EM_DASH}" > "${r20}/loose.md"
printf 'nothing: in scope\n' > "${r20}/notes.txt"
git -C "${r20}" add notes.txt > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "git tree with no tracked file in scope" 0 "${r20}"

# 21. Matching stays case-insensitive in a git tree, not only when walking.
r21="$(new_repo)"
printf 'metadata:\n  description: "%s node"\n' "${BANNED_GPU}" > "${r21}/config.yaml"
git -C "${r21}" add config.yaml > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
run_case "tracked banned device phrase in a git tree" 1 "${r21}"

#
# Failure to run is not success.
#

# 22. A root that is not there cannot be reported clean.
run_case "root does not exist" 2 "${WORK}/no-such-directory"

# 23. A file in the index but missing from disk makes grep fail. A checker that
# cannot read what it was told to read has not found the tree clean.
r23="$(new_repo)"
printf '# Notes\n\nNothing forbidden here.\n' > "${r23}/gone.md"
git -C "${r23}" add gone.md > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 2
rm -f "${r23}/gone.md"
run_case "tracked file missing from disk" 2 "${r23}"

echo
if [ "${failures}" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "${failures} of ${cases} cases failed"
    exit 1
fi
echo "all ${cases} cases passed"

.PHONY: build fmt verify test coverage lint ci-lint vendor mod-tidy mod-vendor mod-verify check-vendor licenses release-snapshot mdlint

CONTAINER_RUN_CMD ?= docker run
GO_CMD ?= go
GO_FMT ?= gofmt
GO_SRC := $(shell find . -type f -name '*.go' -not -path "./vendor/*" -not -path "./dist/*")
CONTAINER_RUN_CMD ?= docker run

BINARY_NAME ?= kubectl-nv

VERSION := 0.1.0

build:
	@rm -rf bin
	$(GO_CMD) build -o bin/$(BINARY_NAME) cmd/main.go

fmt:
	@$(GO_FMT) -w -l $(GO_SRC)

COVERAGE_FILE := coverage.out
test:
	go test -coverprofile=$(COVERAGE_FILE) ./cmd/... ./internal/...
coverage: test
	go tool cover -func=$(COVERAGE_FILE)

verify:
	@out=`$(GO_FMT) -l -d $(GO_SRC)`; \
	if [ -n "$$out" ]; then \
	    echo "$$out"; \
	    exit 1; \
	fi

ci-lint:
	golangci-lint run --timeout 10m

lint:
	golangci-lint run --timeout 10m
	bash hack/lint-words_test.sh
	bash hack/lint-words.sh

vendor:  | mod-tidy mod-vendor mod-verify

mod-tidy:
	@for mod in $$(find . -name go.mod -not -path "./testdata/*" -not -path "./third_party/*"); do \
	    echo "Tidying $$mod..."; ( \
	        cd $$(dirname $$mod) && go mod tidy \
            ) || exit 1; \
	done

mod-vendor:
	@for mod in $$(find . -name go.mod -not -path "./testdata/*" -not -path "./third_party/*" -not -path "./deployments/*"); do \
		echo "Vendoring $$mod..."; ( \
			cd $$(dirname $$mod) && go mod vendor \
			) || exit 1; \
	done

mod-verify:
	@for mod in $$(find . -name go.mod -not -path "./testdata/*" -not -path "./third_party/*"); do \
	    echo "Verifying $$mod..."; ( \
	        cd $$(dirname $$mod) && go mod verify | sed 's/^/  /g' \
	    ) || exit 1; \
	done

check-vendor: vendor
	git diff --exit-code HEAD -- go.mod go.sum vendor

licenses:
	go-licenses csv $(MODULE)/...

release-snapshot:
	goreleaser release --snapshot --clean --skip=sbom

mdlint:
	${CONTAINER_RUN_CMD} \
	--rm \
	--volume "${PWD}:/workdir:ro,z" \
	--workdir /workdir \
	ruby:slim \
	/workdir/hack/mdlint.sh
